notes: Act 1 (HB1001) and Act 2 (SB1) of the 2026 First Extraordinary Session, signed May 6, 2026, cut the top individual rate from 3.9% to 3.7% for tax year 2026 and later. DFA's HB1001 fiscal impact statement gives the 2026 standard income table: 0% to $5,599, 2% $5,600-$11,199, 3% $11,200-$15,999, 3.4% $16,000-$26,399, 3.7% $26,400-$94,700. DFA had not posted official 2026 tax tables when checked (the 2026 AR1000ES worksheet still shows the pre-cut 3.9% schedule).
Arkansas uses the same rate table for every filing status (joint filers apply it to combined income or may file separately on the same return).

Above $94,700 of net taxable income Arkansas uses the upper income table (2026: 2% on the first $4,700 and 3.7% above, i.e. tax = 3.7% x NTI - $79.90 once NTI exceeds $97,600), with bracket adjustments phasing it in between $94,701 and $97,600. Modeled as a recapture of the lower brackets' benefit phased in over $2,900 of NTI (state AGI thresholds assume the $2,470-per-taxpayer standard deduction); the model then taxes all NTI at 3.7%, overstating tax by about $80 above $97,600 of NTI.
Low-income tax tables (which can reduce tax to zero for low incomes) are not modeled.

Standard deduction ($2,470 per taxpayer) is the 2025 figure; DFA's 2026 AR1000ES worksheet also uses $2,470. Personal tax credits are $29 per taxpayer ($58 for joint and head of household); dependent, age 65+, blind and deaf credits of $29 each are not modeled.
Arkansas does not allow the deductible half of self-employment tax.

seDeduction.note: Arkansas computes its own AGI; the AR1000ADJ adjustment list does not include the deductible half of SE tax.

seHealthInsurance.note: Self-employed health insurance deduction is an allowed adjustment on Form AR1000ADJ.

retirementContributions.note: KEOGH, self-employed SEP and SIMPLE plan contributions are allowed adjustments on Form AR1000ADJ.

qbi.note: Arkansas does not start from federal taxable income and has no QBI deduction.

localIncomeTax.note: Arkansas cities and counties do not levy local income taxes.

estimatedTax.threshold: Required if you can reasonably expect 2026 Arkansas tax after credits and withholding to be more than $1,000.
estimatedTax.safeHarbor: Estimated payments must be at least 90% of the tax actually due; otherwise a 10% per-annum underestimate penalty applies. The penalty is computed on the lesser of the current year's or the previous year's tax liability (Form AR2210).

businessCosts.llcFormationFee: $45 online ($50 paper) Certificate of Organization (Form LL-01), Arkansas Secretary of State.
businessCosts.annualReportFee: $150 Annual LLC Franchise Tax Report, due every year on or before May 1 (first report due May 1 of the year after formation).
businessCosts.franchiseOrMinimumTax: The $150 annual LLC franchise tax (paid with the annual report) is the only entity-level charge for an LLC.
businessCosts.grossReceiptsTax: None on income. Arkansas's 'gross receipts tax' is its sales tax, which applies to tangible goods and specifically enumerated services only.
